public_rationale: Meta has announced an AI-video feed and development of a new character experience. Neither cited announcement establishes the return of Meta-operated character profiles on Facebook or Instagram. No decisive event satisfying the early-resolution rule was verified by October 28, 2026. With no stated deadline, the forecast remains open.
limitations: Searches cannot prove that an unpublicized or limited test never occurred.
A successor product counts only if it restores the relevant public-profile functionality.
Evidence for more AI content does not by itself prove the chatbot forecast or its causal explanation.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Meta's deleted AI chatbot profiles will return, because Meta intends to fill feeds with AI-generated or AI-summarized content.

statement.excerpt: I am 100% sure that these chatbots will return, because it's fairly obvious that Meta intends to fill your feeds with content either entirely generated or summarized by generative AI, be it with fake profiles or content itself.

from_speaker: Meta intends to fill your feeds
entirely generated or summarized by generative AI
our_interpretation: 'These chatbots' refers to Meta's withdrawn character profiles on Facebook or Instagram.
A restoration of those profiles or a clear successor offering of Meta-operated character profiles would count; identical names are not required.
A general assistant, user-created chatbots or an AI-content feed alone would not establish their return.
The statement about Meta's intentions is the forecast's rationale, not an antecedent that must occur before it can be scored.
criteria.support_condition: A dated, publicly documented restoration or successor launch makes Meta-operated AI character profiles available on Facebook or Instagram after the post.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive event permanently makes such a return impossible. Continued nonappearance or a reversible cancellation does not establish failure of an undated forecast.
